title: Tesla AI5 ve AI6 çip bellek kapasitesini düşürdü
summary: Tesla, seri üretimi güvenceye almak amacıyla AI5 ve AI6 çiplerinin bellek gereksinimlerini önemli ölçüde azalttı.
body:
Wccftech'in aktardığına göre, Tesla'nın kurucusu Elon Musk, **Tesla AI5** ve AI6 çiplerinin bellek kapasitelerinde indirime gidildiğini duyurdu. Piyasada yaşanan bellek tedarik kısıtlamaları nedeniyle yapılan bu değişikliğin, şirketin insansı robotu Optimus'un performansını etkilemeyeceği belirtiliyor. Çipler; Tesla'nın otonom sürüş sistemleri ve Optimus robotları için güç kaynağı olarak tasarlanıyor.

## Bellek kapasiteleri yarıya indirildi

Alınan kararla birlikte, daha önce 144 GB olması beklenen AI5 çipinin belleği 72 GB LPDDR5 seviyesine çekildi. AI6 çipinin bellek kapasitesi ise yaklaşık üçte oranında bir azalışla 144 GB LPDDR6 olarak güncellendi. TSMC ve Samsung tarafından 2 nanometre teknolojisiyle üretilmesi planlanan AI5 çipinin deneme üretimi Samsung'un Teksas'taki tesislerinde sürerken, seri üretime 2027 yılında geçilmesi öngörülüyor.

**Neden önemli?** Küresel bellek sıkıntısı, çip tasarımı yapan dev üreticileri üretim hacmini korumak adına donanım özelliklerinde fedakarlık yapmaya zorluyor.

source_texts.text:
In what is a testament to the chronically constrained supply of memory right now, Elon Musk has just announced a significant de-spec for Tesla's AI5 and AI6 chips just to secure volume production for these chips.
Elon Musk asserts that the AI5 and AI6 de-spec won't affect the performance of Tesla's Optimus humanoid robot
Elon Musk has just announced that Tesla's AI5 and AI6 chips are getting a memory downgrade, with the former reduced to 72 GB of LPDDR5 while the latter now expected to sport 144 GB of LPDDR6, which constitutes a reduction of around one-third.
For the benefit of those who might not be aware, Tesla intends to use its AI5 and AI6 chips to power its FSD-geared compute stack and the Optimus humanoid robot.
As a refresher, Tesla's AI5 chip sports a half-reticle physical size, and features a large primary die in the middle that handles all of the compute and 12 DRAM modules on the periphery. The chip will be fabricated at TSMC and Samsung on the 2nm node, and offer 2000-2500 TOPS. The single-chip variant is roughly equal to NVIDIA H100 GPUs while the dual-chip configuration is able to head-to-head with Blackwell. Finally, while the chip was initially expected to sport 144 GB of LPDDR5, Musk has just curtailed its memory content to 72 GB. Trial production for this chip is already underway, at Samsung's Taylor facility in Texas, with volume production expected in 2027.
What's more, the AI6 and AI6.5 chips are also expected to retain TSMC and Samsung as the fabrication hubs, while sporting copious amounts of SRAM. Elon Musk noted in April: "Both chips have ~half of the TRIP AI computation accelerators dedicated to SRAM, so effective memory bandwidth is an order of magnitude greater than DRAM bandwidth for any calculations in SRAM cache." Of course, the DRAM component has now been slashed by a third to 144 GB.
Finally, as we noted on Wednesday, Micron now believes that each humanoid robot will require around 200 GB of DRAM and multiple terabytes of NAND, with the memory giant going on to add during its earnings call that "physical AI can become a significant driver of memory and storage demand by the end of this decade."
